correctness.rationale: For 0<p≤1 and positive weights, fiber disjointness gives ||Tx||_p^p=Σ_n λ_n^p|w_nx_n|^p, proving boundedness exactly when sup λ_n<∞. For t>σ_j, at most j−1 columns exceed t; coordinate truncation yields a_j,c_j,d_j≤t and dimension-intersection gives b_j≤t. For s<σ_j choose j columns λ_n>s; their span gives b_j,a_j,c_j≥s. The nonstandard Kolmogorov lower bound is justified: for normalized pairwise disjoint z_i, approximants f_i in a lower-dimensional F with ||z_i−f_i||_p^p<1 imply strict column p-mass diagonal dominance D_ii>Σ_{r≠i}D_ri. Any dependence Σα_i f_i=0 contradicts p-subadditivity after summing each block, since Σ|α_i|^pD_ii≤Σ|α_i|^pΣ_{r≠i}D_ri. Thus some z_i has distance at least 1 from F; d_j≥s. Supremum/nonattainment, λ=0 and j arbitrary are handled. Compactness follows from finite-coordinate truncation, whereas nonvanishing infinite λ selects an infinite-dimensional coordinate subspace where T is bounded below, so compact/strictly singular/finitely strictly singular are equivalent. The source examples and finite verifier are corroborative only.
